clue.text: Remodelled sports ground a second time

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public sports field

explanation.surface: A stadium is redeveloped for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a second time' reads as one phrase meaning again; it is three separate pieces. REC is British shorthand for a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast something is to give it a new form, so remodelled is a synonym.

clue.text: Formula ready for use city area gets brought in

indicators.note: the city area is brought into the middle of the word for ready, splitting it

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to be eaten
EC is the postcode district for the City of London

explanation.surface: A ready-made formula is brought into use in some part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the London postal district covering the City.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set formula of ingredients and steps for producing a dish or result.

clue.text: Argued prisoner should get looked after

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
tended means cared for or looked after

explanation.surface: Someone argued that an inmate deserved proper care.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to assert or maintain in argument, so contended is a synonym of argued.

clue.text: Female is capsizing in something riddled with holes

indicators.note: in a down clue, capsizing turns the pieces upside down, so they are read from the bottom up

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, stands for a female

explanation.surface: A woman overturns in a boat full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve is a mesh utensil, perforated all over so liquid or fine material passes through.

clue.text: Had meal at back of pub? That's natural

indicators.note: says the eating word follows the pub word in the answer

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Eating in the back room of a pub is the most natural thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn rather than learned, which is what natural means here.

clue.text: Residents show up, going in opposite directions

indicators.note: the reversed show goes into the gap between the two compass points

parts.note: north and south are opposite compass points, N and S

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical

explanation.surface: Local people turn out, heading off different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a noun here, a stage musical, not the verb in 'show up'; in this down clue 'up' reads it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are people born in a place, so they are its residents.

clue.text: A party creating a fuss

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A party gets noisy and causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means bother or commotion, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Attempts to participate in games — say, skittles

indicators.note: the answer takes part in these words, sitting inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Trying to join in sports, skittles for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in gamES SAY Skittles.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an old word for an attempt or trial, as in essaying a task.

clue.text: Ann's voice, sort proving tricky in discussions?

indicators.note: the letters prove awkward to keep in order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ann's voice turns out hard to deal with in debates.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversations are spoken exchanges, so they are discussions.

clue.text: Number in competition observed going round

indicators.note: the word for observed goes round the competition word

parts.note: seen means observed
an event is a sporting competition

explanation.surface: A number of entrants in a contest were watched closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a particular number, so the definition is a general term for it.

clue.text: Bit of food delivered to church

parts.note: a pie is an item of food
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Some food is brought to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of food' reads as one phrase; 'Bit' alone is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment, so a bit.

clue.text: Little girl, as one doing nothing in a brilliant way

parts.note: Viv is a short form of the girl's name Vivian
idly means in the way of someone not doing anything

explanation.surface: A young girl lazes about, but brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivid means bright and intense, so vividly is a brilliant manner.

clue.text: Malign a girl initially praised, turning nasty

indicators.note: the letters turn, changing into a new order
only the first letter of girl is used

explanation.surface: Someone slanders a girl who was first praised, then turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: A, G and PRAISED are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to belittle them, so it is a synonym of the verb malign.

clue.text: Describes as evil different characters from Des Moines

indicators.note: the letters of the city name are made into a different word

explanation.surface: Someone paints the people of Des Moines, the Iowa capital, as wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonise is to portray someone as a demon, so as wicked.

clue.text: To catch horse, frenzied dame ran

indicators.note: the jumbled lady's letters catch, holding, the horse word inside
frenzied means wild, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: a nag is a horse, often an old one

explanation.surface: A wild woman ran to catch a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frenzied' turns DAME into MAED, which holds NAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a business is to run it, so managed means ran.

clue.text: Mother and boy cursed

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mother and her son swore.
explanation.definitionFit: The damned are those condemned by a curse, so the adjective cursed fits.

clue.text: After drinks editor gets made fun of

indicators.note: the editor comes after the drinks in the answer

parts.note: teas are drinks

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, the editor gets mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to mock or poke fun at someone, so teased is a synonym.

clue.text: An Italian poet's musical movement

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet; the 's links him to the definition

explanation.surface: A piece of music written by an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a moderate tempo marking, and a movement of a work often takes it as its name.

clue.text: Tree that goes high up into the sky

definitions.meaning: a broad-leaved tree common in city streets

definitions.text: that goes high up into the sky
definitions.meaning: an aeroplane climbs high into the sky

explanation.surface: A tree that grows so tall it seems to touch the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Plane names both the tree and, for short, an aircraft.

clue.text: Former president is human being without the first bit of sense

indicators.note: without means one letter of the word for human is taken away

parts.note: a person is a human being

indicators.note: only the first letter of sense is used

explanation.surface: A former leader is described as a person with no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan Perón was president of Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Perón was a former Argentine president, so the answer is an example.

clue.text: So Nana and Grannie could be very old people

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: Nana and Grannie might be extremely old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link: SO, NANA and GRANNIE alone give the thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonagenarians are people in their nineties, so very old people.

clue.text: No pay, no work? No!

indicators.note: no here means the letters for work are absent from the joined pieces

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A worker protests: no pay means no work, full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Join NO and PAY, then take out OP to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old or formal word for no.

clue.text: Nymphs being dull and awfully sad

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nymphs who are boring and terribly unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryads are tree nymphs of Greek myth.

clue.text: Surely that could be denied

indicators.note: the word could be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: Surely that claim could be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic word of agreement, like certainly or surely.
